_meta.indication: SIMPONI is a TNF blocker indicated for treatment of adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (in combination with methotrexate), active psoriatic arthritis (alone or with methotrexate), and active ankylosing spondylitis.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, controlled trial comparing Simponi 50 mg and 100 mg with background MTX vs background MTX monotherapy, administered subcutaneously monthly for 24 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adult RA patients with inadequate response to MTX ≥ 15 mg weekly
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of ACR20 responders at Week 14; co-primary endpoint of improvement from baseline in HAQ-DI at Week 24
pivotal_trials.n: MTX + pbo n=133; Golimumab 100 mg monotherapy n=133; Golimumab 50 mg + MTX n=89; combined golimumab n=178
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 14: golimumab 50 mg + MTX 55% vs MTX + placebo 33% (p=0.001); combined golimumab 56% (p<0.001)

nct_ctgov.title: An Efficacy and Safety Study of Golimumab in Patients With Active Rheumatoid Arthritis Despite Methotrexate Therapy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study C0524T11 (T11), RA, prior TNF inhibitor use
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized trial of Simponi 50 mg, 100 mg, or placebo administered subcutaneously monthly for 24 weeks as adjunctive therapy with background DMARDs
pivotal_trials.population: RA patients with inadequate response to DMARDs and a history of previous TNF inhibitor use
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of ACR20 responders at Week 14
pivotal_trials.n: DMARDs + pbo n=155; Golimumab 50 mg n=153; Golimumab 100 mg + DMARDs n=153; combined golimumab n=306
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 14: golimumab 50 mg 35% vs DMARDs + placebo 18% (p<0.001); combined golimumab 37% (p<0.001)

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Golimumab (CNTO 148) in Subjects With Active Rheumatoid Arthritis Previously Treated With Biologic Anti-TNFa Agent(s)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized trial of Simponi 50 mg, 100 mg, and placebo administered subcutaneously monthly with or without background MTX for 24 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with active psoriatic arthritis, with or without concomitant background MTX
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of ACR20 responders in the combined Simponi group at Week 14 compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo n=113; Golimumab 50 mg n=146; combined golimumab n=292
pivotal_trials.result: ACR20 at Week 14: golimumab 50 mg 51% vs placebo 9% (p<0.0001); combined golimumab 48% (p<0.0001)

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Golimumab in Patients With Active Psoriatic Arthritis

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized trial of Simponi 50 mg, 100 mg, and placebo administered subcutaneously monthly with or without background DMARDs for 24 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with active ankylosing spondylitis, with or without concomitant background DMARDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects in the combined Simponi arms achieving an ASAS 20 response at Week 14 compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo n=78; Golimumab 50 mg n=136; combined golimumab n=278
pivotal_trials.result: ASAS 20 at Week 14: golimumab 50 mg 59% vs placebo 22% (p<0.0001); combined golimumab 60% (p<0.0001)

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Golimumab in Subjects With Active Ankylosing Spondylitis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%) were upper respiratory tract infection (7% vs 6% control) and nasopharyngitis (6% vs 5% control). Serious risks include serious infections including tuberculosis, invasive fungal and other opportunistic infections, malignancies including lymphoma, heart failure, and demyelinating disorders.
target_moa: Golimumab is a human monoclonal antibody that binds both soluble and transmembrane forms of human TNFα, preventing TNFα from binding to its receptors and thereby inhibiting its biological activity.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS. Patients treated with SIMPONI are at increased risk for serious infections leading to hospitalization or death, including active tuberculosis, invasive fungal infections, and bacterial, viral and other opportunistic infections; SIMPONI should be discontinued if a serious infection develops.

rems.type: A REMS was required, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments, to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks of serious infections, malignancies, congestive heart failure and peripheral demyelinating disorders.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the product is a member of the TNF-blocker class and the safety and efficacy data did not pose unique concerns.

summary.text: Standard full approval of a TNF-blocker monoclonal antibody BLA received June 24, 2008 and approved April 24, 2009, supported by five Phase 3 trials, with a required REMS; no advisory committee was convened as the product is a member of the TNF-blocker class.

citations.quote: We have approved your biologics license application for Simponi (golimumab) effective this date April 24, 2009.
The sponsor has submitted the results from five Phase 3 clinical trials in support of the efficacy of Simponi for RA, PA and AS.

Your application for Simponi (golimumab) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because your product is a member of the class of tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-blockers, and the safety and efficacy data did not pose unique concerns beyond those applicable to other biologic products in the TNF-blocker class approved for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.

requirement.text: Required deferred pediatric study under PREA: assess the pharmacokinetics, safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy of golimumab in pediatric patients 2 to 16 years of age with active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA).
